data.title: Clindamycin phosphate 1% gel
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Lincosamide antibiotic (topical)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit → inhibits bacterial protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
- Reduces C. acnes and the free fatty acids it produces; anti-inflammatory (reduces neutrophil chemotaxis)
- Phosphate ester is inactive until hydrolysed in the skin

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Inflammatory acne vulgaris (papules, pustules) — always combined with benzoyl peroxide (BPO) to prevent resistance
- Folliculitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (mild, Hurley I), rosacea (alternative), pitted keratolysis, erythrasma
- Also in the anti-acne list (group VII)

## Dose & formulations
- Thin layer once or twice daily
- Fixed combinations: clindamycin 1% + BPO 2.5–5%; clindamycin 1.2% + tretinoin 0.025%; clindamycin + adapalene; clindamycin + nicotinamide
- Do not use as monotherapy and limit to about 12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Dryness, peeling, irritation
- C. acnes and staphylococcal resistance with monotherapy
- C. difficile colitis is very rare (case reports)

## Contraindications
- History of inflammatory bowel disease or antibiotic-associated colitis
- Hypersensitivity to lincomycin/clindamycin

## Drug interactions
- Erythromycin topical — antagonism (both act at 50S)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy (preferred topical antibiotic with BPO).

## Viva points
- Never use topical antibiotics alone for acne — always with BPO (resistance)
- Safe in pregnancy
- Rare pseudomembranous colitis — ask about bowel disease

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41 (Topical antibacterials); Khopkar ch.18. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
